scope: Matched real critical-window evaluation of the final rank-8 flower-task VACE checkpoint
summary: The stronger adapter still fails all four semantic gates and regresses control-motion alignment, so the workflow again rejects full 27.5-second expansion.
evidence: Inference reused the same real input, control, edit mask, reference, prompt, seed 20260811, 20 steps, denoising strength 0.75, and 448x256x17 protocol.
Outside-edit similarity improves from 0.921049 to 0.921482, a delta of +0.000434.
Control-motion alignment falls from 0.356812 to 0.345687, a delta of -0.011125.
Uniform review of frames 0, 4, 8, 12, and 16 finds retained human head/torso, fragmented robot geometry, no two coherent hands, no causal stem contact, and no persistent flower-identity evidence.
evaluation.json records 0/4 semantic gates and REJECT_FULL_EXPANSION.
lessons: Increasing LoRA rank and optimization steps on the same small synthetic distribution does not close the real embodiment/contact gap.
The critical-window gate prevented a longer but scientifically unsupported output.
limitations: The edit mask uses flower-union evidence rather than persistent stem instances.
This one 17-frame window cannot establish long-horizon quality.
next_actions: Use paired real robot/action data and persistent object instances before another adaptation attempt.
